sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Export Distribution of Pre-Packaged Spicy Tallow Hotpot Base Bricks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
United States-Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 11 May 1991)
Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 April 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Régimen Jurídico de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended; Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT preventive measures), as amended by Ley 70 de 2019; Decreto Ejecutivo 129 de 20 de marzo de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales implemented at the Registro Público de Panamá); regulations of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) of Panama and GAFILAT standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or national civil registry of the founder's country of origin (notarized in the country of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the Circuit, Republic of Panama, or foreign notary if lawfully executed abroad and authenticated under applicable private international law rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Panama (for outbound verified use) or Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Panamanian law firm acting as Resident Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Panama; Hague Apostille for outbound banking or commercial counterparty use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the counterparty's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of the founder, Foundation Council members, beneficiaries, and connected trading counterparties against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Panamanian UAF domestic designations; politically exposed persons (PEPs), including close associates and family members, are subject to enhanced due diligence, beneficial-ownership substantiation, and written risk assessment under Ley 23 de 2015, as amended, before the foundation charter may be executed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Personas Jurídicas / Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado; name pre-registration and certificate application available through the official Registro Público online administrative portal (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa) and E-Tablón system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be composed in the Latin alphabet, must end with or include the statutory denomination 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Foundation', must be distinctive, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in the Registro Público de Panamá. A foreign-language name is permissible only where it is rendered in Latin script, correctly transliterated, free of typographic symbols or punctuation not recognized by the registry, and accompanied by the statutory denomination; Spanish and English names are preferred for registry processing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant or its Resident Agent must file a written Recurso de Reconsideración before the Dirección General of the Registro Público de Panamá within ten business days of written notification, attaching supporting trademark or ownership evidence where applicable; if reconsideration is denied, an Apelación may be lodged with the superior administrative hierarchy of the Registro Público, and ultimate recourse lies in a Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa filed before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory judicial review period. A fresh name reservation (with full re-filing fees) may also be submitted while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute for the statutory registered seat. A Panama Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office and a licensed resident agent (law firm) with a physical office in the Republic of Panama; a virtual office or online administrative address may at most serve ancillary communication functions and cannot replace the statutory Resident Agency or the registered office address recorded in the Registro Público.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% per annual compliance cycle for a standard low-risk wholesale export distribution foundation; probability increases to an estimated 25–35% if UBO information discrepancies, PEP exposure, or adverse sanctions-screening hits are detected, triggering unannounced on-site inspections by the UAF or the Registro Público de Panamá.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundation Law), as amended by Decree-Law 5 of 2015 and Law 254 of 2021, applicable Articles 1-36; residual application of Ley 32 de 1927 (General Law of Corporations) for procedural matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Deed of Incorporation of a Private Interest Foundation), or equivalent private instrument, subject to mandatory registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No mandatory statutory minimum capitalization under Ley 25 de 1995; the foundation charter must declare an initial endowment sufficient for the stated purpose. For this export distribution vehicle, a declared initial endowment of US$10,000, held in a Panamanian escrow account by the Registered Agent, is adopted to satisfy banking, licensing, and due-diligence requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]. The Founder and the initial members of the Foundation Council, acting by unanimous written consent under the Private Interest Foundation Law, hereby RESOLVE: (1) the initial endowment of the Foundation is fixed at US$10,000, which sum shall be remitted by the Founder to the escrow account established by the Registered Agent; (2) the registered office of the Foundation is established at the office of the Registered Agent in Panama; (3) the following officers are appointed: [name], President; [name], Secretary; and [name], Treasurer; and (4) the President and Secretary, jointly, are authorized to execute and file all documents necessary to obtain the export distribution license, open bank accounts, and otherwise manage the operations of the Foundation. Adopted at the Foundation's registered office on [insert date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Personas Jurídicas (Oficina Virtual)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a corporate name search against registered entities to ensure the proposed trade name does not conflict. Submit Form for Name Reservation (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre) with the Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado; the reservation is valid for 30 days (renewable). For private interest foundations, the name must include the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' or the abbreviation 'F.' as required by law.
required_dossiers: Copy of the Founder's passport or corporate ID
Power of attorney if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected due to similarity, file a written rectification request and select a revised secondary name; a new search within the same application is not subject to an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Review of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Panamanian legal counsel and Notario Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A Panamanian attorney drafts the Escritura Pública or private foundational document, including the foundation's name, initial endowment, purpose, governance rules, registered agent appointment, and beneficiary provisions. The draft is circulated to the founder's counsel for approval, then executed before a Notary Public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary issues observations, the attorney may submit a revised draft without additional government fees; re-notarization may require a new signature by the founder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público de la República de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule a notarial appointment. The Founder, or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact, appears before the Notary to sign the Escritura Pública. The Notary certifies the signature and legality of the act. The executed deed is then forwarded to the Public Registry for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial execution is defective, the deed can be corrected by an 'Aclaración o Corrección' before the same Notary or via a certiorari before the Public Registry, depending on materiality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarized foundation deed, together with the paid fee, to the Registry's foundations section. The Registry assigns an entry number, reviews the deed for legality and conformity, and issues the Certificate of Registration and copies of the marginal note. The foundation becomes a distinct legal entity upon registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'reparo' (observation), the law firm responds with an amendment or clarification within the granted term; if the correction is unaccepted, a written appeal can be lodged with the Registry Director within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Municipal Operation License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and the Municipality of the registered address (Alcaldía)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the certificate of incorporation is issued, the foundation must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from DGI by filing the 'Formulario de Registro' and attaching the constitutional documents. If the foundation carries on commercial activities, the municipality requires an 'Aviso de Operación' for the physical premises. For an export distribution operation, the RUC must include the customs-exporter activation code.
required_dossiers: Proof of physical address (lease or sale contract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the application for missing information, file a 'subsanación' response via the DGI e-window; for municipal license denials, appeal to the Alcalde's office within the prescribed 15-day period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institution (licensed Panamanian bank) and the Foundation Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting of the Foundation Council (or accept the pro-forma First Board Resolution). Approve the resolution adopting the registered office, ratifying the initial endowment, and appointing the founding officers. The bank will conduct due diligence, requiring certified copies of the registration and a notarized bank mandate. The council minutes and resolution are recorded in the foundation's minutes book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the signatory structure, the Foundation Council may pass a supplementary resolution to appoint new signatories, and the registry entry will be updated accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección General de Industrias y Comercio
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Sanitaria para Alimentos y Registro de Establecimiento de Alimentos (Sanitary License and Food Establishment Registration, Ministerio de Salud - MINSA), complemented by the municipal Aviso de Operación

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I - Environmental Registration (Registro) only, not a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), because the operation consists of storage, labeling, and distribution of pre-packaged goods with no meat processing or rendering. A Category III full EIA is triggered only if production or rendering of animal fat is introduced at the premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater and sanitary discharges must meet Panamanian discharge standards (pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 100 mg/L, COD not exceeding 250 mg/L, and total suspended solids not exceeding 100 mg/L). Spicy tallow bricks are to be stored at ambient temperature under sealed food-grade packaging to prevent odor emissions; any spill must be immediately contained and remediated in accordance with DGNTI-COPANIT standards. Solid hygiene waste shall be disposed through a licensed municipal or private hauler. No significant VOC or air pollutant emissions are expected from the pre-packaged product handling; cleaning solvents must be used under controlled protocols to remain below regulatory thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Certificado de Prevención de Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering egress, fire extinguishers, and storage of combustible tallow; structural safety and occupancy clearance from the Municipality; and occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) and the Social Security Fund (CSS).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online portal: SISTEMA T@-PANET and Sede Electrónica (https://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panamanian Private Interest Foundation must first register its Foundation Charter with the Public Registry of Panama, file the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) with the Municipal Treasury, then obtain a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from DGI via the T@-PANET portal. Where the PIF derives only foreign-source income, the RUC is nonetheless required for export invoicing and potential ITBMS credit recovery; a resident legal representative must be appointed. The application requires a notarized foundation charter, certified identity documents, proof of registered address, and payment of the inscription fee; issuance typically occurs within 5-10 business days after Public Registry inscription.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or full entity-reclassification election exists under Panamanian law. A PIF may elect voluntary ITBMS registration even below the B/.36,000 turnover threshold to claim input VAT credits on export purchases, and may file an annual Solvency/Income Affidavit (Suelto de Renta) confirming that all income is foreign-source and thus outside Panama's territorial income tax. Hybrid mismatch elections are unavailable under domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a VAT-equivalent levy administered by DGI
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Panamanian Balboa, pegged 1:1 to USD 36,000) of gross annual taxable turnover; exporters may register voluntarily to recover input ITBMS credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Ley 66 de 2020 and DGI resolutions on SEDI (Sistema Electrónico de Facturación) / T@-PANET. Taxpayers must issue XML-based e-invoices with digital signature, QR verification, an AIU fiscal ID code, and obtain a real-time DGI digital authorization code before clearance. Export invoices must bear the 'Exportación' type code and reference the supporting customs declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A PIF exporting pre-packaged hotpot soup-base bricks qualifies for the 0% ITBMS rate when (i) the goods are physically shipped out of Panamanian customs territory, (ii) title and risk transfer to a non-resident buyer, (iii) the export is evidenced by an authorized customs registry, and (iv) the transaction is recorded in the DGI electronic system. Corresponding input ITBMS on local purchases becomes refundable (crédito fiscal) via Form 401 filed electronically through T@-PANET.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed via VUPE/SIUCA with DGI validation
Bill of Lading (ocean or air waybill) showing Panama as port of origin
Inward Remittance Certificate and commercial invoice evidencing payment from the foreign buyer
Packing list and certificate of origin for the seasoning base product line
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may retroactively reverse zero-rated export credits, assess 7% ITBMS plus monthly interest (1.5% per month), and impose fines of up to 100% of the understated tax for documentary deficiencies. False export declarations trigger criminal tax-fraud liability under the Código Penal (Ley 14 de 2007) carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years, exclusion from the exporter registry, and customs confiscation penalties ranging from 5 to 15 times the merchandise value in aggravated customs fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no conventional central bank. Banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under the banking law framework (Decreto Ley 9 de 1998), while Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as the fiscal agent of the State. No exchange-control authority or central-bank approval exists for foreign-exchange transactions, capital flows, or trade settlements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the United States dollar is legal tender and the balboa circulates only as 1:1 USD-pegged coinage. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible, with no restrictions on profit repatriation or dividend remittance. The PIF's foreign-source trading income falls under Panama's territorial tax system and may be distributed to non-resident beneficiaries without Panamanian withholding tax; the only practical frictions are banking KYC/AML compliance, not currency convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or conversion requirement on export proceeds; exporters may retain and freely dispose of 100% of USD and foreign-currency receivables. The PIF must hold a valid RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), register the export-wholesale activity with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), and file shipment-level export declarations with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas, but no central-bank clearance certificate or conversion mandate applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with trade-finance and LC limits

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Global Bank Internacional, S.A. (Global Bank Corporation)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low viability as the primary rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer) are not licensed by the SBP to provide payment services in Panama and their internal client policies generally exclude private interest foundations from business-account onboarding. SBP-licensed domestic e-payment companies can hold USD client funds, but their limits and trade-finance capabilities are insufficient for LC-backed procurement of hotpot base from China. EMIs should therefore be used only for small B2B disbursements, never for the initial capital injection or documentary-credit settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default requirement at all tier-1 banks: at least one Foundation Council member (typically the president) must attend a face-to-face onboarding interview in Panama City, and the resident agent (a licensed Panamanian attorney or law firm) must provide a compliance comfort letter. Remote opening is possible only through private-banking and wealth units, which may accept reinforced video-KYC combined with apostilled and notarized certified copies of the charter, reglamento, and council resolutions; banks treat this as an exception under SBP customer due diligence rules (Ley 23 de 2015), so plan for 5-10 business days in-person versus 2-4 weeks remote.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Confidential PIF legal form: council members and beneficiaries not on the public registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original registered Certificado de Constitución from the Public Registry; voluntary filing of the Reglamento and council minutes; signed UBO declaration mapping each natural person to the USD 1,000,000 patrimony; resident agent Carta de Cumplimiento confirming good standing and payment of the annual USD 350.00 foundation fee (Ley 25 de 1995, as amended).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident entity flagged as substance-less or shell-like during correspondent-bank review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of real trading activity: signed master supply agreement with the Sichuan (CN) hotpot-base brick manufacturer; pro-forma invoices and purchase orders from Latin-American distributors; warehouse or logistics contracts in Panama or Colón Free Zone; DGI RUC registration; Aduanas exporter profile; and a formal Foundation Council resolution approving the export-trading programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacque source of wealth and source of funds for the initial USD 1,000,000 capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements and tax clearance of the founding beneficiary for the preceding 24-36 months; bank reference letters issued less than 30 days before onboarding; sworn statement of lawful origin; the notarized Aporte de Patrimonio deed; and the downstream trade contracts demonstrating commercial use of the injected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: China-to-LatAm trade route and animal-fat food product perceived as elevated counter-party risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening pass for all Chinese and Latin-American counterparties; Chinese supplier business-registration extract and HACCP/ISO-22000 food-safety certificates; MINSA import registration and sanitary certificates for the pre-packaged hotpot base; and a consistent customs audit trail across the PIF's export declarations and corresponding bills of lading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Single irrevocable SWIFT MT103 wire from the beneficiary's corporate account at Bancolombia (Bogotá) to the PIF's USD operational account at Banco General (Panama City) using the purpose-of-payment field 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation patrimony under Ley 25 de 1995'. The receiving bank requires the foundation charter, the Aporte de Patrimonio deed, and the source-of-funds bundle before crediting; USD credits clear through the US correspondent Fedwire/CHIPS network, so same-day value is achieved for instructions received before 13:00 Panama time. Cash deposits of USD 10,000 or more generate automatic UAF filings, making wire-based injection the preferred compliant route.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: China procurement leg: 30% of the purchase price prepaid via SWIFT MT103 and 70% through an irrevocable sight documentary Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 series) opened by Banistmo or BAC through New York correspondents in favor of the Chinese supplier's bank (Bank of China), with shipment and expiry dates aligned to the factory production schedule. Latin-American distribution leg: MT103 TT wires in USD to buyers' accounts at Bancolombia and BAC Credomatic, supported by commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and Panama Customs export declaration. Panama USD clearing depends on the US correspondent system (Fedwire/CHIPS); domestic Panama payments settle through the local ACH, and once released all TTs are irrevocable, so documentary compliance must be verified before settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH outright forwards (tenor 1-12 months) available from Panama-licensed global and international banks (Citi, Itaú Unibanco Panamá, Bancolombia Panamá) to hedge CNY-denominated payables to the Chinese hotpot-base supplier
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY where onshore CNY deliverability is unavailable to the PIF, cash-settled in USD against CNH reference fixes
USD/CNH cross-currency swaps under a standard ISDA/CSA collateral arrangement for commitment periods matching the commercial LC payment schedule
Vanilla USD/CNY call options and collar structures to cap conversion cost on large, uncertain procurement volumes

No USD/balboa- or USD/local-currency hedge is required because Panama is fully dollarized; all hedge documentation must be supported by the master supply agreement and the LC schedule to satisfy bank compliance review

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Fee (Anualidad de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de la República de Panamá; payments coordinated through the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; a grace period until 30 April is available with the statutory surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a surcharge of 10% of the fee per month or part of a month (minimum USD 10) plus statutory interest; failure to pay for two consecutive years permits the Registro Público to suspend the foundation's legal personality, revoke registration, and proceed with administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Personas Jurídicas; Beneficial Ownership Registry Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each annual registration anniversary; the declaration must be filed each year regardless of changes in ownership or beneficiary status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late submission after prior notice triggers administrative fines ranging from USD 1,000 to USD 10,000, and may cause the registration record of the foundation to be flagged; persistent non-compliance supports judicial suspension or strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return / Informative Tax Filing (Declaración de Renta Anual) for Commercial Activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the following fiscal year for taxpayers with calendar-year books; if the foundation's books are approved on a different fiscal year, the deadline is the last day of the calendar month following the fiscal-year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing carries a fine of 5% of the tax due for the first month and 1% for each additional month, with a minimum fine of USD 100; inaccuracies can attract penalties of 15%–25% of omitted tax, and chronic non-filing permits DGI to issue a tax deficiency, seize bank accounts, and request deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Commercial Operation Renewal (Renovación del Aviso de Operación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal; District Municipality where the foundation maintains a commercial establishment, if any
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the month of January, or no later than 31 March for renewals applicable to the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Renewal after the deadline incurs a late surcharge of 20% of the unpaid fee; continued failure to renew triggers municipal closure of the commercial establishment, administrative fines, and loss of the municipal operating permit

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is compulsory for a Panama Private Interest Foundation that exclusively engages in foreign-source distribution activities and does not generate Panama-source revenue; an independent certified audit becomes mandatory when annual gross receipts exceed USD 1,000,000, when the foundation is placed in a tax-loss situation, when DGI orders an audit, or when a commercial lender/investor agreement requires audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; foundations engaged in taxable commercial activity must prepare financial statements under IFRS, while foundations without taxable Panama-source activity may maintain simplified internal records

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The foundation must keep an internal record of beneficial owners and submit an annual confirmation declaration to the Registro Público, disclosing the current foundation council, protector, beneficiaries, and any persons who can direct the foundation's assets or operations. There are no shares or capital stock in a Private Interest Foundation; disposal of beneficial interest is effected by an amendment to the foundation charter or foundation regulations, which must be notarized and registered with the Public Registry. Any annual change in the beneficiary schedule triggers an updated confirmation filing within the same annual declaration window
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registry of Protector Appointments and Resignations
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 4,000 per certified audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies: income sourced in Panama is taxable at 25%; income sourced outside Panama is exempt if it is not derived from activities carried out within Panama and does not give rise to Panama-source receipts. Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are not subject to income tax on foreign-source commercial income, provided all logistical, contractual, and substantive business acts occur outside Panama. No general export tax holiday is available for traditional packaged-food exporters, but deductions for direct costs, depreciation, and documented operating expenses reduce the effective rate. The optional SME simplified regime applies only when gross Panama-source income does not exceed B/. 200,000 and may yield a progressive rate of up to 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1503 – Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return); filed electronically through the DGI e-SEDE portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministry of Economy and Finance).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and full payment are due no later than 15 March of the year immediately following the close of a calendar-year corporate fiscal period. Non-calendar fiscal years require filing within three months of the fiscal year-end and the formal permission of the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (Registro Único de Contribuyente) of the Private Interest Foundation or its registered legal entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Panama PIF must first obtain a RUC through the DGI’s online registration portal; foreign-owner identifiers are disclosed on a separate registry attachment, not in the public RUC field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The 12-month fiscal period to which the return relates (e.g., 01.01.2026 to 31.12.2026).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with no Panama bank account or local operating office must still select the periodic calendar-year box and attach the official minutes designating the fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue deriving from commercial, industrial, or business activities performed in Panama, including distribution of hotpot base to purchasers when title transfer and risk of loss arise in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income generated from a Panama-located trade or business. If the purchase order, payment, and delivery risk occur entirely outside Panama, the income should not be included here; provide a reconciliation note in the appended annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income arising outside Panama and not attributable to a Panama permanent establishment or Panama-located business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners of a PIF should instruct management to file this line as zero only if the PIF holds no assets or personnel in Panama; otherwise, an explanatory exhibit is required to defend the territorial exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Acquisition or production costs of pre-packaged soup-base bricks that were sold, including inward freight, customs duties, and direct manufacturing costs only for entities engaging in physical transformation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must substantiate costs with invoice-level microscopy of the supply chain; linked-party import costs must be adjusted to arm’s-length prices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after cost of sales, allowable operating deductions, depreciation, and any carryforward loss deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers should ensure that administrative and management fees paid to foreign related parties are deducted only when evidence of actual service is present and the rates satisfy the arm’s-length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount obtained by applying 25% to the net taxable income shown in Box 19.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No exemption is allowed for distributions or shareholder tokens; compute the rate strictly on the Panama-source taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax liability after subtracting quarterly advance payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must remit any balance due by bank wire to the DGI collection account before 15 March; a late remittance triggers daily interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty equal to 5% of the tax shown due, plus 1% for each month or fraction of a month of delay, capped at 25% of the tax. Late payment: a 10% late-payment surcharge plus monthly interest at the current bank lending rate charged by the National Bank of Panama. Failure to file the return also suspends the issuance of tax clearance certificates and can lead to a forced assessment based on period deposits and asset transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 1504 – Declaración de Pagos Parciales (Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Advance Return); filed through the DGI e-SEDE portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly advance tax declarations are due on or before 15 April, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for calendar-year taxpayers. Each quarter’s payment is calculated using prior-year taxable income adjusted for the official price index.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Code designating the three-month calendar quarter to which the advance payment relates (e.g., 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must use the same fiscal-period code selected in Form 1503 and do not have the authority to change the reassessment period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The prior year’s net taxable income, adjusted upward by a price index and any legal modifications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign entities must recalculate the base using the Florida-style CPI adjustment published by the DGI; using an unadjusted base is a trigger for recalculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The effective rate of 25% applied to the adjusted taxable base, with prior quarterly advances credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The standard 25% rate is not reduced by any treaty article for corporations; treaties affect only final dividend or royalty withholding, not quarterly advances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount due for the quarter after subtracting amounts previously paid on Form 1504.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled PIFs must ensure the advance is paid in the RUF or USD through an authorized bank, attaching the DGI online receipt to the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 1504: a fine of B/. 50 to B/. 1,000 depending on the amount of gross income, plus a 10% surcharge on the unpaid quarterly advance and monthly interest. Failure to file all four quarterly returns invalidates the taxpayer’s ability to claim prior payments as offsets in the annual Form 1503.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on any dividend, distribution, or economic-distribution paid by a Panama-domiciled entity from Panama-source profits. The rate applies to resident and non-resident shareholders alike, and the distributing PIF is the statutory withholding agent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a small number of double tax agreements (e.g., with Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, and Barbados), most of which are pending full entry into force. To invoke a treaty-reduced rate, the beneficial owner must file a DGI Form 2229 before the payment date, attach a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence jurisdiction, an ownership declaration, and documentary proof of legal entitlement to the income. Abstention from withholding requires a favorable DGI ruling in correct form, normally issued within 30 working days. Without this administrative protocol, the 10% dividend withholding is applied in full.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of patents, trademarks, know-how, or industrial processes in Panama are subject to a 12.5% statutory withholding tax when the payment is deductibly linked to Panama-source revenue. Interest paid to a non-resident lender on a loan secured by Panama assets or invested in a Panama business is subject to a 5% withholding rate; interest derived by foreign financial institutions from purely foreign funding arrangements is normally exempt. Treaty relief, where available, may reduce the rates to 5% on royalties and interest, but the same Form 2229/TRC process controls the exemption.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be contemporaneously prepared when annual related-party transactions exceed B/. 3,000,000 (USD 3,000,000). A Master File is mandatory for taxpayers forming part of a multinational group with consolidated group revenue equal to or greater than B/. 50,000,000 (USD 50,000,000). Any taxpayer with annual gross revenues above B/. 12,000,000 must maintain structured TP documentation even if the volume of related-party operations is lower.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama’s Economic Substance Regulations apply to entities that are resident in Panama and carry on one or more relevant activities. The export distribution of pre-packaged food items qualifies as a ‘distribution and service center’ activity, so the PIF must demonstrate in its Panama territory: (i) a physical office where core income-generating decisions are made; (ii) at least one full-time employee with sufficient qualification and competence; (iii) actual expenditure in Panama lawfully proportionate to the revenue; (iv) substantive board or foundation council meetings held in Panama; and (v) proper records and governance documentation evidencing the local direction of operations. A PIF that engages in inter-company purchase and resale of hotpot soup base while being managed entirely abroad is considered a shell and will be re-characterized for Nexus Tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately excluding Panama-sourced distribution income from Form 1503, fabricating invoice dates or warehouse documentation, creating backdated purchase agreements for soup-base bricks, or inflating foreign expenses to reduce the 25% taxable base to near zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction of 50% of the omitted tax up to three times the amount owed; criminal tax evasion under Panama’s Tax Procedure Law carries imprisonment from 2 to 5 years, monetary penalties equal to the tax evaded, and forfeiture of forged documents and related assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The courts may pierce the foundation veil when the founder and directors act as mere formalities; directors are then personally liable for the evasion debt, subject to bank account freezes, judicial attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and entry into the DGI/public prosecutorial blacklist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Substantive Presence Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF with no physical office, no local employees, no Panamanian board minutes, and no bank account in Panama while recording the same cross-border distribution transactions as the hub of an export chain; appointing foreign nominees who sign on the PIF’s behalf without actual management oversight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Economic Substance Regulations range from a mandatory administrative fine of B/. 10,000 to B/. 500,000, plus potential late-interest at the statutory rate; the PIF registry may additionally cancel or suspend the foundation registration for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are held jointly and severally for the ESR fines. During investigation, the Public Registry and DGI may impose exit bans on the registered director, and the courts may attach the director’s personal assets for the unpaid fine if the foundation lacks separate funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Trade-Based AML Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the pre-packaged hotpot soup base export as a vehicle for trade-based laundering: invoicing substantially more than actual product quantity, undervaluing the commodity to move currency abroad, commingling illicit proceeds with legitimate revenue, and failing to conduct customer due diligence or to report suspicious Cross-Border Electronic Transfers (Salei) to the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to B/. 1,000,000 per violation for the PIF and its compliance officer; criminal sanctions for money laundering under Law 23 of 2015 include imprisonment from 3 to 5 years (aggravated up to 10 years), cumulative monetary penalties, and forfeiture of all accounts and warehouses tied to the hotpot base transaction chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and foundation directors are treated as principals by the UAF and Public Prosecutor’s Office; they face criminal indictment, passport suspension, exit bans, personal restitution orders, civil forfeiture of their personal property, and, upon conviction, maximum prison term enhancement for acting in the name of a private-interest vehicle.
